transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-27 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Aventis CTO), Liam O'Connor (Aventis ML Eng), Sofia Martinez (Aventis Platform)
Links: benchmark sheet: https://redwood.sheets/aventis-poc-benchmarks (shared), security packet: https://redwood.docs/sec-aventis (shared)

Summary (auto): quick wins on batching and cache reduced median latency, p99 still slightly higher than baseline on their small batch workload, plan dedicated H100 runs and follow-ups.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we have the updated runs to walk through, uh Carlos will kick off with the numbers
00:18 Carlos: cool yeah I pulled the sheet, so quick overview — we ran three profiles: hosted default (gpt-like 8k), tuned batching+cache, and dedicated H100 with quantization. baseline provider (BaseCloud AI) numbers are in the right-most columns for comparison, dev note: their runs were on A100-80gb rumored setup so keep that in mind
00:44 Priya: quick question before you start, the baseline numbers are from their public docs or from our runs?
00:51 Carlos: these baseline are from your shared artifacts — I took the csv you provided (the week one export) and re-ran a subset to match payload size. there might be small mismatches cause of tokenization differences, I tried to normalize
01:10 Carlos: ok median latency for our tuned hosted run is 220ms per request (single-turn, 128 tokens). baseline median is 260ms, so we beat them on median. throughput for tuned is ~42 req/s for the worker pool test, baseline reported 38 req/s
01:34 Liam: hmm those numbers look good but what's the p99? that's what bites us in prod
01:38 Carlos: right so p99 for tuned hosted is 1.2s, baseline p99 reported is 980ms — so baseline is better at tail in this particular distribution
01:52 Sofia: is that because of caching? we have a lot of repeated prefixes in prod traffic so cache should help right
01:58 Carlos: yeah exactly — our KV prefix cache helps median a bunch but doesn't always help p99 if there's a cold start or very long prompt that goes through the full path. we saw a pattern where cold KV loads + batch flushes cause a tail
02:16 Maya: also worth noting hardware differences. on the baseline runs they used A100 with static batching, our hosted environment had mixed GPUs. when we moved to a dedicated H100 pool the p99 dropped to 740ms for the same workload
02:33 Priya: you saw 740ms on H100? that's a big delta, can you repeat that number and the config?
02:39 Carlos: sure — dedicated H100, quantized int8 profile q8_3, batch target 8, adaptive batching with 20ms latency cap, KV cache enabled. in that config median was 180ms, p95 360ms, p99 740ms, throughput ~65 req/s in continuous test
02:59 Liam: interesting, the quantization profile didn't impact quality much on our eval set? we flagged hallucination risk on q8 for some of our prompts
03:07 Carlos: we ran rouge/accuracy evals against your prompt set — small uptick in hallucinations (<1.5% delta) for q8_3 vs fp16 on the long context prompts. for short prompts it's negligible. we can iterate on per-route quant settings so sensitive flows stay fp16
03:25 Priya: ok that per-route idea is helpful. what's the cost delta on H100 + q8 vs baseline A100 they quoted?
03:32 Maya: rough numbers: H100 dedicated config increases infra cost ~1.3x vs their A100 public price but token cost efficiency improved because throughput is higher; net unit cost was about 0.9x for many workloads. we'll send a breakdown in the sheet
03:48 Sofia: can you explain the batch sizing effect again — we saw worse p99 when batch target was 32
03:54 Carlos: yeah larger batches increase throughput but they exacerbate tail for latency-sensitive requests because we hold requests to fill the batch; adaptive batching with a tight latency cap (e.g. 20ms) helps tradeoff — smaller effective batch for tails, larger when busy. we tuned for 20ms cap and target 8 which got the best p99/throughput balance
04:20 Liam: what about model variant fallbacks — if we run out of capacity do we have automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model?
04:26 Maya: yes, routing policies can fall back to a smaller model family or to lower-fidelity quantized variant; that is configurable per-route with SLO-based thresholds
04:36 Priya: security question — are logs encrypted at rest and can we integrate our KMS?
04:40 Maya: yes logs and customer data are encrypted and you can bring-your-own KMS for Private deployments. for hosted we have HSM options and we can share SOC2 artifacts — I'll attach them after the call
04:53 Sofia: perfect. back to numbers, can we see per-model token throughput? meaning tokens/sec across long context runs
05:00 Carlos: sure for the tuned H100 run tokens/sec peaked ~2100 tokens/s, baseline A100 peak ~1500 tokens/s on your sample; sustained was lower depending on sequence length distribution
05:18 Liam: that matches our expectations. we typically have 30% long-context (>2048) traffic which might reduce effective throughput
05:25 Carlos: right and quantization helps more for shorter sequences; for very long context large KV cache and offloading helps a lot, we're experimenting with segmented KV loading to avoid stalls
05:38 Priya: can you walk through the pipeline — where are the main latency contributors in your instrumentation?
05:43 Carlos: sure — breakdown on our trace: request ingress ~12ms, tokenization ~8-10ms, model execution median ~140ms tuned, KV cache hits reduce model exec by ~45%, kernel launch/compilation for cold models ~80-200ms (that's the big variable for p99), network hop to storage for cold KV ~60-120ms when it happens
06:12 Sofia: kernel compilation — can we pre-warm or persist kernels for our dedicated pool?
06:16 Carlos: yes persistent warm pools are the standard for Dedicated; we can pin model builds so compilation doesn't happen on first request. that eliminates a large portion of the tail
06:30 Priya: good — for our pilot we want to minimize cold paths. Liam will provide the request histogram by tomorrow
06:36 Liam: yep I'll drop that in the sheet, expect it by EOD tomorrow
06:41 Maya: great, action item noted.
06:45 (short silence, crosstalk)
06:50 Carlos: one more data point — when we enabled prefix caching with a larger LRU size the median dropped by another 10% but memory usage per instance went up; for Dedicated we have more headroom so it's worthwhile
07:06 Priya: what's the memory delta roughly?
07:09 Carlos: about +18% RAM and KV cache footprint; on H100 we had spare, on older A100 it's tighter so tuning needed
07:18 Sofia: any change to SLO if we do more aggressive caching? we need guarantees for multi-tenant behavior
07:23 Maya: we can set tenant-level memory caps and eviction policies; Redwood Console shows per-route memory and cache hit rate so ops can monitor and enforce
07:34 Liam: curious if you saw any significant differences in diverse prompt types — chats vs single-turn API calls
07:39 Carlos: chats benefit more from KV because of repeated context; single-turn gains mostly from batching. in our tests chat median improved ~30% with cache on repeated prefixes
07:50 Priya: ok let's talk about next run — we want a dedicated H100 test with our real request histogram, not synthetic. timeline?
07:57 Maya: we can spin a daily dedicated run next Tuesday if we lock the dataset and grant access to the env; Carlos can provision the pool and prep the images
08:06 Carlos: yep, I'll create the dedicated pool and provide a docker image; need your sample traces and tokens distribution. also confirm the model version to pin — you said v2.1?
08:15 Liam: yes v2.1 for the pilot, but we may want v2.2 in a canary later. start with v2.1
08:20 Maya: noted. I'll also include a quantization recommendation per-route to avoid the hallucination risk Liam mentioned
08:26 Priya: on the perf sheet your p99 numbers for hosted tuned vs baseline — there was a row where our baseline beat Redwood, any idea why that outlier exists
08:34 Carlos: looking — that was from a mixed workload with very low concurrency; baseline uses a micro-batch scheduler that avoids kernel churn in that oddly-sparse pattern, our default adaptive batching had a slightly different idle flush heuristic which caused a few slow extra compiles; fixed by tuning the idle flush to 40ms in that run
08:55 Sofia: thanks, good catch. can we get both configs in the sheet so we can replay?
09:00 Carlos: yes I'll add run ids and exact config flags.
09:04 Priya: one more on SSO — we need SAML + SCIM for provisioning, timeline for those docs?
09:09 Maya: I'll share SAML/SCIM integration guide and we can do a short onboarding call with security once you review; target to have SAML sample in a week
09:17 Liam: ok for acceptance criteria — our VP wants p99 < 800ms on median production histogram and per-token cost <= baseline+10%. is that doable?
09:27 Maya: achievable on Dedicated H100 with the tuning we described; per-token cost should be comparable or slightly better due to improved throughput, we'll provide a cost model with sensitivity analysis
09:36 Priya: perfect. final quick items — can you surface any vendor lock-in risks?
09:41 Carlos: minimal; we support model format portability and you can run in Private or Dedicated; routing abstracts model variants so you can fall back to baseline provider if needed during rollout
09:50 Maya: ok let's recap next steps.
09:53 Maya: Carlos will update the benchmark sheet with run ids, full p95/p99 columns, and config flags by 2026-03-30.
09:59 Maya: Liam will provide traffic histogram and target SLOs by 2026-04-02.
10:04 Maya: I'll send SOC2/security pack and SAML/SCIM guide by 2026-03-29.
10:10 Priya: thanks all, this was helpful.
10:13 Sofia: thanks!
10:15 Meeting end.
